description:
FILED s415 with #371's measurement.

The Track A refusal for given/when costs exactly two files their whole run,
because a transpile-time die yields no TAP at all:
  perl-tests/state.t   158 passing -> 0   (one `given` block at line 350 of 616)
  t/op/state.t         126 passing -> 0   (the same file in perl's own t/)
Everything else the five families touch was already unproductive
(t/op/switch.t 27 C_ok of 169 rows, t/class/*.t 0-1, t/op/defer.t 0,
t/op/coreamp.t 0, the format files 0).

This cost is NOT caused by Track A: at the end of Option B phase 2 the emitters
flip from announce to DIE for EVERY remaining drop (fable-answers-s400.md Â§6.4),
and `given` will still not be implemented then -- so state.t was going to refuse
either way.  Track A only brings it forward, and it buys the honest answer for
every USER program that uses the removed feature.

Rows left docs/pass-baseline.tsv ROW BY ROW in s415 with this cause; the
companion snapshot rows are registered as expected divergences.

REVISIT ONLY IF: a third file with real coverage joins them, or a CPAN
distribution PCL needs uses given/when (none does -- it is removed in 5.42).
Implementing given/when as a lowering (given = a topicalizing block binding $_,
when = a smart-match-free equality test + implicit `last`) is possible but would
also require the smart-match semantics `when` implies, which is the actual
reason perl removed it.
subject: state.t (both populations) loses every row to the #371 given/when refusal -- the trade recorded; revisit only if a third file with real coverage appears
